A1.justification: Both 33-page PDFs describe SATURN and contain matching main sections, references, checklist, and Appendices A–L. Full-text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable comparison; differences are confined to pages 1 and 10.

before.justification: v3 reports original SATURN training and evaluation results on SATURN-2.6k and reasoning benchmarks, including baseline comparisons, ablations, and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains the original SATURN experiments, numerical benchmark results, ablations, and qualitative analyses in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: Section 2 and Appendices A–B retain the same SAT constructor, adaptive curriculum, difficulty-based progression, GRPO objective, and reward scheme.

E1.justification: Both retain the same SATURN-2.6k coverage and AIME, AMC, MATH-500, GPQA Diamond, and LiveCodeBench tasks. The harder SAT scenarios in Appendix I are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain identical baseline membership, including distilled-Qwen and SFT baselines, Logic-RL and ScaleQuest in Tables 2–4, and the CDCL solver in Appendix I.

E3.justification: Section 3.2 and Appendices A and D–F report identical data splits, model configurations, training budgets, evaluation metrics, decoding settings, and prompts. No experimental protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: The difficulty-estimator ablation in Appendix C, curriculum and sampling ablations in Appendix H, and error/reasoning analyses in Appendices I–J are unchanged. Appendix L retains the same word-cloud analysis.

E5.justification: Sampling counts, Table 7's standard-deviation reporting, and the checklist's statement that explicit error bars are not reported remain unchanged. No new run/seed information or uncertainty-estimation procedure appears.

E6.justification: Numerical results, rankings, plots, and qualitative findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 3 retains average scores of 48.2 for SATURN-1.5B and 63.4 for SATURN-7B.

T1.justification: The SAT definition, difficulty estimator, and mathematical development are unchanged, including Equations (1)–(3) and Appendix C's assumptions and derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about scalable, verifiable, difficulty-controlled SAT training, curriculum learning, and transfer to other reasoning tasks.

C2.justification: The self-verification interpretation and discussions of transfer remain unchanged. Section 4 retains the same limitations involving plateauing gains, domain knowledge, context windows, plasticity, and forgetting.

D1.justification: The implementation pseudocode, hyperparameter tables, hardware disclosures, prompt templates, and documented code/data/model access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 5, Appendix K, and all 54 reference entries are unchanged. The positioning relative to constructed reasoning tasks and earlier SAT-based evaluations is retained.

P1.justification: v4 removes the symbol after Jia Li's name, updates the arXiv version/date stamp, and adds Beijing Natural Science Foundation grant 4264107 to the acknowledgements. Scientific prose and document organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: There are small author-block alignment changes on page 1 and reduced vertical spacing on page 10 to accommodate the extended acknowledgement. Figures and tables are unchanged; the other 31 pages render identically.

improvement.justification: v4 adds a funding credit and removes an author-name symbol, with minor local layout adjustments. The scientific arguments, empirical evidence, limitations, and reproducibility information remain unchanged, so these administrative and presentation edits do not materially affect overall paper quality.
